name: Waikaremoana
metered: The metered history has one meter for Tuai, Piripaua and Kaitawa together, so it shows the scheme whole. The dispatch data (the live week and the weeks since the newest metered month) shows each station.

about.text: The Waikaremoana Power Scheme in northern Hawke's Bay runs water from Lake Waikaremoana through three stations in turn: Kaitawa, Tuai and Piripaua. Tuai opened first, in 1929, making this the North Island's second government hydro scheme after Mangahao; Piripaua followed in 1943 and Kaitawa last. Kaitawa was the first to draw straight from the lake, through tunnels in the ancient landslide dam that formed it; before then the stations used only the water that leaked or spilled out. Tuai has the highest head and makes the largest share of the scheme's power.

facts.label: Commissioned
facts.note: Genesis's lake history gives 1949 for Kaitawa (see notes)

facts.label: Units
facts.value: 7 units: Tuai 3 of 20 MW, Piripaua 2 of 21 MW, Kaitawa 2 of 18 MW

facts.label: River or lake
facts.value: Lake Waikaremoana and the Waikaretaheke River
facts.note: Kaitawa draws from Lake Waikaremoana and discharges into Lake Kaitawa, Tuai's head pond; Tuai discharges into Lake Whakamarino, Piripaua's intake

facts.label: Owner
facts.note: Genesis Energy Limited, named Genesis Power Limited when it took the scheme over in 1999

facts.label: Previous owners
facts.value: New Zealand Government, to 1987; Electricity Corporation of New Zealand (ECNZ), 1987–99
facts.note: ECNZ took over the Crown's generation on 1 April 1987; the split directions of March 1999 moved Kaitawa, Tuai and Piripaua to Genesis Power Limited (now Genesis Energy), from 1 April 1999

facts.label: Stations
facts.value: Kaitawa (36 MW), Tuai (60 MW), Piripaua (42 MW)
